blocks.text: CSS Centering Images
Centering Images
With CSS, you can center images with several methods.
An image can be centered horizontally, vertically, or both.
Center an Image Horizontally

To display a horizontally centered image, we can use
margin: auto; or
display: flex;.
1. Using margin: auto
One way to center an image horizontally on a page is to use margin: auto.
Since the element is an inline element by default (and margin: auto does not have any effect on inline elements) we must convert the image to a block element, with display: block.

In addition, we have to define a width. The
width of the image must be smaller than the width of the page.

blocks.text: 2. Using display: flex
Another way to center an image horizontally on a page is to use  display: flex.

Here, we put the element inside a
container.
We add the following CSS to the div container:

items: justify-content: center (centers the image horizontally in the div container)

blocks.text: Then, we set a width for the image. The width of the image must be smaller than the width of the page.

blocks.text: Vertical and Horizontal Centering

To display an image that is both vertically and horizontally centered (true
centering), we can use display: flex; or display:
grid;.
1. Using display: flex

To display an image that is both vertically and horizontally centered with
flexbox, we use a combination of:

items: justify-content: center; (centers the image horizontally in the container)
align-items: center; (centers the image vertically in the container)

Here, we also put the element inside a
container.

Then, we set a width for the image (must be smaller than the
width of the container).
